While this isn't strictly consoles, it did release during the last generation so here goes:

Two Things

First:

The reworking of Final Fantasy XIV into FFXIV: A Realm Reborn (which also released on PS3), an astounding feat considering they did it in two years, and it remains one of the few profitable subscription based MMOs. I fondly remember getting up at 4:30 am in prep for the server launch, making a cup of coffee and some toast, and plunking down at my desk. Pumping myself up with my favorite final fantasy tunes I watched the sunrise, and entered what remains one of my favorite gaming worlds to date.

Second:

Discovering The Witcher series. If you love RPGs, these games are a must play. While the original Witcher game is quite clunky (and PC exclusive), I feel it is really important to play as it helps inform the world, and makes the latter two games all that more enjoyable!

Gears of War. I bought this the day it came out, and I played it coop with 2 of my friends for several complete weekends in a row. We just kept beating the game over and over on progressively more difficult settings. Since there were 3 of us and coop was 2 player we would just swap out whenever we got tired. The best part was, my friends would go out of their way to break the game and do crazy bullshit. Charge at the enemy and try to just blind fire the sniper rifle at them? Why not? Try to lure enemies into krill spots that instantly devour them? I dub thee the Krill Gun! We just had an amazing time.

For me, the Might and Magic series was the breakout memory. Each installment had something to offer that wasn't necessarily an improvement over prior episodes. MM3 for instance, was the first to have modern first-person movement...not to mention a great twist ending! MM4 and 5, if installed together on the same hard drive would combine to form a larger connected world, as well as a special "third ending" once you complete the individual games. MM6 was the best overall story and open world experience. In fact, I'm playing MM6 now on my Retro game YouTube channel. UbiSoft now owns the rights to the series and continues to make episodes. Sadly, the series is on UPlay only...no Steam support yet.
